topic: Acute medical unit function and flow

audits.title: A day in the life of the AMU--the Society for Acute Medicine's benchmarking audit 2012 (SAMBA '12).
audits.standard: Society for Acute Medicine common standards, including timing of junior and senior review; high reliability defined as over 90% compliance
audits.setting: 30 acute medical units (Society for Acute Medicine national audit)

cycle1.result: Compliance with timing of junior and senior review was highly variable; for almost all other standards only a small number of units achieved over 90% compliance.

audits.other_findings: Mean 36 (SD 14) admissions per unit; annual audit suggested.
audits.citation: Subbe CP, Ward D, Latip L, Le Jeune I, Bell D. A day in the life of the AMU--the Society for Acute Medicine's benchmarking audit 2012 (SAMBA '12). Acute Med. 2013;12(2):69-73. doi:10.52964/amja.0289. PMID: 23732129.

audits.title: "State of the Nation"--the Society for Acute Medicine's Benchmarking Audit 2013 (SAMBA '13).
audits.standard: Society for Acute Medicine clinical quality indicators

cycle1.result: 76% had early warning score within 30 minutes of admission; 95% seen by a competent decision maker within four hours; 79% seen by a consultant within the appropriate time.

audits.citation: Le Jeune I, Masterton-Smith C, Subbe CP, Ward D. "State of the Nation"--the Society for Acute Medicine's Benchmarking Audit 2013 (SAMBA '13). Acute Med. 2013;12(4):214-219. doi:10.52964/amja.0321. PMID: 24364052.

audits.title: Relationship between input and output in acute medicine - secondary analysis of the Society for Acute Medicine's benchmarking audit 2013 (SAMBA '13).
audits.standard: Society for Acute Medicine published quality indicators for timely assessment and discharge
audits.setting: 43 acute medical units on a single day (SAMBA '13)

cycle1.result: Performance against quality indicators was worst in the early evening; units admitting fewer than 40 patients performed better.

audits.other_findings: Frailer patients (Clinical Frailty Scale) had more physiological abnormality and higher NEWS.
audits.citation: Subbe CP, Burford C, Le Jeune I, Masterton-Smith C, Ward D. Relationship between input and output in acute medicine - secondary analysis of the Society for Acute Medicine's benchmarking audit 2013 (SAMBA '13). Clin Med (Lond). 2015;15(1):15-19. doi:10.7861/clinmedicine.15-1-15. PMID: 25650192.

audits.title: The Team at Work--The Society for Acute Medicine's Benchmarking Audit 2014 (SAMBA'14).
audits.standard: Society for Acute Medicine clinical quality indicators and Royal College of Physicians standards (early warning score within 30 minutes, competent decision maker within 4 hours, timely consultant review)
audits.setting: 66 acute medical units in the UK (SAMBA 2014)

cycle1.result: 84% had an early warning score within 30 minutes, 81% were seen by a competent decision maker within 4 hours and 73% saw a consultant in time; only 56% met all three standards.

audits.other_findings: No relation was found between unit characteristics or staffing and performance.
audits.citation: Subbe CP, Le Jeune I, Burford C, Mudannayake RS. The Team at Work--The Society for Acute Medicine's Benchmarking Audit 2014 (SAMBA'14). Acute Med. 2015;14(3):99-103. doi:10.52964/amja.0441. PMID: 26767198.

audits.title: Restoring the core acute medical unit (AMU) function - a quality improvement initiative from a district general hospital.
audits.standard: National guidance and GIRFT principles for acute medical units
audits.setting: Acute medical unit, Frimley Park Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: National benchmarking and local audit showed core acute medicine processes had drifted from standards (no figures given).

audits.intervention: Real-time oversight, standardised multidisciplinary board rounds and rota alignment to peak demand.

cycle2.result: AMU length of stay halved, daily discharges doubled and ED-to-AMU transfers increased.

audits.other_findings: Improvements were associated with better hospital-wide throughput.
audits.citation: Wijewardane A, Dyer P. Restoring the core acute medical unit (AMU) function - a quality improvement initiative from a district general hospital. Future Healthc J. 2025;12(4):100486. doi:10.1016/j.fhj.2025.100486. PMID: 41438169.
